summary:
Marcus Bell is dry rehearsal sergeant who only praises when the room is empty. The life that shows in public is anchored at South Congress music school, Austin. Marcus teaches evening guitar and leaves the side door unlocked during rehearsal. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Patient, dryly funny, and serious about practice. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: they rehearse apologies they have never delivered and the person in front of them now resembles that old mistake. If that truth surfaces at South Congress music school, Austin, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
